caption_en:
The snack almost got cancelled in 1964. 🥜

After a lecture in Tel Aviv, London allergist Gideon Lack noticed how few Israeli doctors had seen a child with peanut allergy. Local parents said their babies eat Bamba, a peanut butter coated corn puff, in their first year (FARE, 2025).
📊 His team compared Jewish schoolchildren: peanut allergy in 1.85% of 5,171 in the UK vs 0.17% of 5,615 in Israel. Israeli babies aged 8 to 14 months ate a median of 7.1 g of peanut protein a month; UK babies, 0 (Du Toit et al., Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology, 2008). That was an observation, not proof.
🧪 The LEAP trial (New England Journal of Medicine, 2015) then fed high risk babies peanut from 4 to 11 months until age 5: up to 81% fewer peanut allergies (FARE). The US NIAID changed its guidance in 2017. In 2024, LEAP-Trio found the protection held into adolescence: 15.4% vs 4.4%, a 71% reduction (King's College London).
🍿 Bamba: Osem launched a cheese snack in 1964 that failed; coating it in peanut butter created Bamba (Israel Hayom, 2025).

⚠️ Bamba isn't medicine. Ask your paediatrician before giving peanut to a baby, especially with eczema or egg allergy.

Did you grow up on Bamba? Tell me below.

Sources: Du Toit et al., JACI 2008; LEAP, NEJM 2015; FARE 2025; NIAID 2017; King's College London 2024; Israel Hayom 2025.

caption_he:
חטיף ישראלי אחד, פי 10 פחות אלרגיות?
אחרי הרצאה בתל אביב, אלרגולוג מלונדון, גדעון לק, שם לב שכמעט אף רופא בחדר לא ראה ילד עם אלרגיה לבוטנים. ההורים אמרו: התינוקות אוכלים במבה בשנה הראשונה.
הצוות שלו השווה ילדים יהודים בבריטניה ובישראל: 1.85% אלרגיה בבריטניה, 0.17% בישראל.
אחר כך ניסוי LEAP: עד 81% פחות אלרגיה לבוטנים. ב-2017 ארה"ב הפכה את ההמלצה, וב-2024 ההגנה עדיין החזיקה אצל בני הנוער.
ועוד משהו: במבה התחילה ב-1964 כחטיף גבינה שנכשל. חמאת בוטנים הצילה אותה.
במבה היא לא תרופה. לפני שנותנים בוטנים לתינוק, מתייעצים עם רופא הילדים.
גדלתם על במבה? כתבו לי.

lines.line: One Israeli snack. Ten times fewer peanut allergies?
Tel Aviv. A London allergist, Gideon Lack, gives a lecture. Very few doctors there have ever seen a child with peanut allergy.
Why? Israeli babies eat Bamba in their first year. Puffed corn, coated in peanut butter.
Bamba launched in 1964 as a cheese snack. It flopped. Peanut butter saved it.
So his team compared Jewish children in Britain and Israel. Same heritage, different snack.
In Britain, 1.85 percent had a peanut allergy. In Israel, 0.17 percent. About ten times fewer.
Then came a real trial, called LEAP: high risk babies, fed peanut from infancy to age five.
The result: up to 81 percent fewer peanut allergies.
In 2017, America flipped its advice. Peanut early, not late.
In 2024, the trial kids were teenagers. Still protected.
Bamba isn't medicine. Ask your paediatrician before a baby tries any peanut food.
Did you grow up on Bamba? Tell me below.
